query: Starting from the 2010 census, how does the Black-White dissimilarity index evolve over 3 steps when a CTA subway station opens in a South-Side tract at step 2, with a paired policy broadcast?
method_notes: Real-world anchored: 2010-census baseline demographics drive P + physical-E; the step-2 transit intervention is modeled on CTA's real South-Side Red Line Extension. Load-bearing magnitudes (city D_bw baseline, Schelling tolerance regime) are sourced; the specific intervention tract and the +2-station shock size are modeling proxies, declared as assumptions.

implementation_refs.title: Schelling, T. (1971) — Dynamic Models of Segregation
implementation_refs.takeaway: Agents relocate when the same-group share of neighbours falls below a tolerance threshold; even mild individual preferences (~30-50%) tip neighbourhoods into sharply segregated macro patterns. This is the decision rule the SchellingDecisionModel implements per household.

implementation_refs.title: Transit-Induced Gentrification: A Quasi-Experimental Analysis of New U.S. Rapid-Transit Stations Opened 2000-2009 (JAPA, 2025)
implementation_refs.takeaway: A new rapid-transit station is a plausibly-exogenous shock to a tract's accessibility; downstream neighbourhood ethnoracial change can go either way (diversifying inflow vs. displacement), motivating the paired anti-displacement broadcast in E and the competing-mechanism framing of the hypothesis.

facts.claim: Chicago metro Black-White dissimilarity index, 2010 census

source.title: Brown University US2010 Diversity & Disparities — Segregation 2010 (Logan/Stults)

facts.note: Chicago is one of the most segregated large U.S. metros; a value of 76 means ~76% of Black or White residents would have to relocate for an even distribution. The study's t=0 D_bw=0.816 is at/above this metro figure because the small-scale South-Side tract subset is more segregated than the metro average.

facts.claim: CTA Red Line Extension — 5.5-mile South-Side rail expansion (95th/Dan Ryan → 130th St)
facts.note: The real South-Side transit shock the step-2 intervention is modeled on: a $5.7B, 4-station extension into historically transit-poor Far South Side communities (ground-broken early 2026). Anchors the direction/plausibility of the intervention, not the exact tract.

facts.claim: Schelling tolerance threshold that still tips a neighbourhood to segregation

source.title: Schelling (1971) + Schelling's Segregation Model: Parameters, scaling, and aggregation (Demographic Research 2009)

facts.note: Bounds the plausible satisfaction-threshold regime for the household decision model.

assumptions.claim: The intervention station is placed in tract 17031612000 (New City, South Side).
assumptions.rationale: A representative South-Side tract in the small-scale subset; the real RLE terminates further south (130th St). Chosen for demonstration — a plausible South-Side transit-shock site, not a claim that RLE serves this exact tract.

assumptions.claim: The station opening is encoded as cta_stations += 2 in the intervention tract at step 2.
assumptions.rationale: No public metric maps a single station opening onto the engine's cta_stations accessibility field; +2 is a deliberate, legible one-off shock large enough to register against the tract's baseline access. Sensitivity to this magnitude is a candidate /sv-iterate sweep.

assumptions.claim: The paired citywide + tract broadcasts describe a fair-housing / anti-displacement program.
assumptions.rationale: Stylized policy text, not a specific enacted Chicago ordinance; represents the counter-displacement lever the transit-gentrification literature argues is needed for a station to diversify rather than displace.
